messages:
morgan: quick sanity-check — proposing a composite canary gate for the new v4q-chat-longcontext bring-up. want to capture quality + cost + latency in one auto-fallback rule.

alex: sounds good. what signals are you thinking?

morgan: combo of: MRR delta (vs baseline), hallucination rate (detected via named-entity hallucination metric), p99 latency uplift, and tokens-per-response cost uplift. each metric normalized to [0,1], then weighted. fallback if score > 0.7 for 10m window.

ravi: +1. are we weighting recall-heavy workloads higher? longdocs tend to see higher latency but small MRR drops.

morgan: yes — we'll allow a seqlen-aware weight. default weights: mrr:0.45, halluc:0.25, latency:0.2, cost:0.1. for >2048 tokens multiply latency weight by 1.5 and mrr by 0.85 (so latency matters more on longctx).

jia: can you paste a draft rollout config? easier to review that way.

morgan: sure — here's the minimal policy we'd give to the orchestration layer:

```json
{
  "policy_name": "fidelity_watchdog_v1",
  "signals": [
    {"name":"mrr_delta","metric":"mrr","direction":"down","normalize":true,"weight":0.45,"threshold":0.06},
    {"name":"halluc_rate","metric":"ner_halluc","direction":"up","normalize":true,"weight":0.25,"threshold":0.03},
    {"name":"latency_p99","metric":"latency_p99_ms","direction":"up","normalize":true,"weight":0.2,"threshold":150},
    {"name":"tokens_cost","metric":"tokens_per_resp_pct","direction":"up","normalize":true,"weight":0.1,"threshold":0.12}
  ],
  "combination": {"method":"weighted_sum","fallback_score_threshold":0.7,"smoothing_window_minutes":10},
  "context_adjustments": [
    {"condition":"seq_len>2048","apply":{"latency_weight_mul":1.5,"mrr_weight_mul":0.85}}
  ],
  "auto_actions": {"on_trigger": ["roll_back","notify:#eng-ml","create_incident_sensitivity:"]}
}
```

alex: small nit: threshold units — latency threshold 150ms p99 seems low for longctx. maybe set absolute p99 threshold to 400ms and use relative uplift too.

morgan: good catch. will change to two-part latency rule: absolute_p99 and pct_uplift (>=20% uplift).

emma: what about false positives from noisy slices? we should require >=3 slices firing or X% of traffic from the canary cohort before auto rollback. otherwise just alert.

ravi: agree. add AND condition: (score>0.7) AND ((canary_traffic_pct>2%) OR (num_slices_firing>=3)).

jia: integration question — can the console show the intermediate weighted contribution per-signal? eg a bar graph for the four signals. ops will want that when they decide manual vs auto.

morgan: yes, telemetry team already exposes per-signal timeseries. we'll wire the UI to compute weighted contribution in real-time.

sre-bot: deploybot: canary rollout started for model:v4q-chat-longctx at 2026-03-23T15:22:00Z (cohort=0.5%). Monitoring hooks: mrr, ner_halluc, latency_p99, tokens_per_resp.

alex: thanks @sre-bot. let's runway this as a soft-autofallback: only auto-rollback for score>0.85 for now, keep 0.7 as an Ops-alert threshold for 24h.

morgan: updated plan: soft-auto = 0.85 (5m sustained), alert-only = 0.7 (10m smoothing), require canary_traffic_pct>=2% OR slices>=3 for auto. I'll push the config to staging and tag @eng-ml for a smoke tomorrow.

jia: sounds good. can you drop the final staged config here when you push? i'll review the UI wiring.

morgan: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

emma: ack. also let's add a small synthetic prompt set that targets halluc-prone entities — will speed signal detection.

morgan: added to the eval harness. starting shadow run against the synthetic set now. will post results 30m.

alex: awesome — appreciate the thoroughness.
